FEAST OF CHRIST THE KING We have been fit for the kingdom by Jesus’s suffering death and resurrection. Like Jesus, we are kingdom kinds of people. And that means that we have the opportunity, through the power of Christ’s cross, to hold together the tensions that life presents to us There are plenty of them to be found. Maybe we aren’t surrounded by rulers and soldiers and criminals; maybe it’s frustrating neighbours and family members with odious political views and classmates who come from different backgrounds. But no matter what hostilities or differences are swirling around us, we, the power of the cross of Christ and not on our own power, can stand in the gap and make peace between parties. Jesus, after all, was able to make peace with his murderers, asking God to forgive them. And as we saw in today’s reading, Jesus promised someone facing death by execution that he would remember him in paradise. In God’s kingdom, no one is forgotten. The cross is strong enough to absorb all the world’s contradictions and make peace between them. We can bring all our inner contradictions to Christ on the Cross. May we, who have been seduced by the mysteries of the cross, follow Jesus and become a sign of peace in our parish and in a world beset by hostilities, misunderstandings, and resentments. CALENDAR FOR THE WEEK AHEAD
Sunday 8th The door is closed against the bridesmaids who did not keep vigil nor trim their lamps.
The concern of the Christian should be readiness for the call of the Lord, to seek the light of Christ in daily living and to keep burning brightly the light received at baptism.
It is true wisdom to be always eagerly longing for the Lord.

Monday 9th Feast of the Dedication of the Lateran Basilica . This church in Rome is known as “the mother and head of all the churches in the city and in the world”. It is the Cathedral Church of the diocese of Rome where Pope Francis is Bishop.
Tuesday 10th Pope St Leo the Great . Pope (440-461).
A gifted pastor and teacher, who intervened decisively at the Council of Chalcedon in 451 in defence of the doctrine of the Incarnation.
Wednesday 11th St Martin of Tours (317-397).
Born in Hungary, educated in Italy, baptized a Christian at the age of 20. Took up the life of a hermit in France and set up the first monastery there.
Thursday 12th St Josaphat (1580-1623). A bishop who worked for the reunification of Christians in Eastern Europe and died a martyr’s death in 1623.
Saturday 14th St Laurence O’Toole (1123-80).
Monk and Abbot of Glendalough, he became Archbishop of Dublin in 1162. He continued the movement of reform begun by Ceallach and Malachy.
He died in Brittany in 1180 while on a mission to restore peace between the kings of Ireland and England.
